title: PSRAM not detected - XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense
body: Also, assumedly related, VLC won't open the stream, though everything builds, uploads and runs correctly (minus PSRAM being detected).
author: slashinpdx

comments.body: Nothing to do with software. Do you have the right board selected in Arduino? No psram is a pio, arduino setting or hardware issue. No camera seems like you have not selected right board in arduino and in code or both.

@slashinpdx In your Arduino IDE, go to Tools > PSRAM > OPI PSRAM. This will get your PSRAM working.

However... While, I also had a successful build and upload, attempts to connect to the RTSP stream fail. I can't figure out why. All the logging suggests everything works, but when it logs `RTSP Address: rtsp://192.168.125.206:554` and I try to go to that address in VLC, it fails to connect to the stream.

Turn on debug log #define RTSP_LOGGING_ENABLED right at the top before include library and constructor also turn on debug logging level debug in the arduino ide tools section. Also it could be a setting in vlc or your router is blocking port 554 most don't
Yeah, for some reason 554 wasn't working. I changed `rtspPort` to `8554` and it worked.

Also, @slashinpdx - I think start with really lowering the quality a lot and then working up to see what works. If your ESP can't keep up with the quality, VLC will just crap out the connection rather than wait for more than 5 seconds. Start with `config.frame_size = FRAMESIZE_128X128;` and `config.jpeg_quality = 63;` to see if you can get _anything_ working.

title: large audio sample causes esp panic
body: `sendRtpAudio()` should check input `len` parameter vs `packet[]` size to avoid buffer overflow panic by chunking as per `sendRtpFrame()`
author: s60sc

comments.body:
Thank you for pointing out the buffer size issue. Initially, I set up the library with a 1024-byte buffer for testing and to ensure correct timestamps. However, I've now implemented a fix that allows audio and subtitles to handle data of any size by fragmenting it into smaller RTP packets. 

I plan to upload the fix in about 10 hours, along with the addition of multi-client support. I was rushing to complete this before returning to work, but rest assured, I'm nearly finished. I'll be sending a pull request for the new multi-client feature, which includes setting a maximum limit for multicast clients and an override for multiple clients across all streaming transports.

Next, I'll be working on secure RTSP (RTSPS) and encryption of the RTP data packets. After these updates, the library should be complete.

Thanks again for highlighting this issue!
Sorry for the delay new version 1.2.0 is out. Now supports multiple clients for multicast or able to overwrite for multiple clients for all transports UDP, TCP, Multicast see in readme

title: The subtitles, they only appear once at startup
author: jhohannfabian

comments.body:
That is strange. I have not noticed any issues with subtitles besides streaming in TCP. The task does the exact same thing as the callback and they both send to the same function. The call back is slower and not as precise as the task so might be losing timestamps. Any way I did notice an issue with the subtitle send function and have fixed also improved TCP streaming, but UDP is a lot better. As this is new and my first library I have created, I am expecting issues. 

PS. New version out v1.10

Oh are you going to the top and activate the subtitles? Should be track 1. I think I know what you mean now. You see the stream address at the start of the video. But no subtitle just active track 1 subtitles. I have taken screenshots of different vlc like how to turn on subtitles and change to TCP but have not added to read me yet. See how you go activating the subtitles track 1, let me know.
